# Open Brand Definition

Project: Open Brand Definition
Specification: OBDS
Current release: 4.1.3 (stable, 12 September 2026)
Publisher: Kill The Dragon GmbH, Vienna, Austria
Canonical address: https://openbranddefinition.org/

Legal notice: https://openbranddefinition.org/legal/

Language: explanatory pages are English. The homepage and legal notice contain
both English and German text in the same HTML; do not treat translations as
separate claims. The legal notice defaults to German without JavaScript.

## Website and evidence boundary

Current explanatory website: 19 September 2026. This website publication is separate
from frozen OBDS 4.1.3 release evidence. The normative specification is unchanged.
Website record: https://openbranddefinition.org/website-publication.json

Ecosystem jobs: DEFINE / STRUCTURE → PUBLISH / DISCOVER → RESOLVE / GOVERN → EXECUTE / VALIDATE.
OBDS sits primarily at RESOLVE / GOVERN. It is not discovery infrastructure, a registry,
an MCP replacement, a renderer or a complete autonomous execution system.
Canonical OBDS truth may have derived human, task-specific, API, MCP and Markdown views;
these are not parallel sources of approved truth or a promise of available adapters.

How it works: https://openbranddefinition.org/what-is-obds/
Use cases: https://openbranddefinition.org/use-cases/
Insights: https://openbranddefinition.org/insights/
Resources: https://openbranddefinition.org/resources/
Ecosystem: https://openbranddefinition.org/ecosystem/

Authoring is non-normative and review-first. Sources are evidence, not approval.
Candidate truth is not approved truth. Automatic ADMIT is not production-cleared.
Research question: Governance completeness before automatic ADMIT. No demonstrated
normative OBDS core gap follows from the supplied Intake/Curation or Sameness learnings.

SUPABRAND ROUND 4 MIXED (tested against OBDS 4.1.2): both submissions 39/40 hidden-case curation points;
93/93 Task Facts replay records agree within the tested boundary; 0/20 complete
end-to-end governed execution for either submission. 0/20 means incomplete pipelines,
not 20 wrong decisions. No universal interoperability or guaranteed on-brand output.
Research: https://openbranddefinition.org/research/
Round 4: https://openbranddefinition.org/research/supabrand/

The comparison separates open specifications/protocols (OBDS, BRAND.md, BCP, MRBS,
Brando) from adjacent products/infrastructure (Sameness), and explains MCP as access
infrastructure. Not a ranking. Documented responsibilities are not implementation proof.

## Definition

OBDS is an open specification with a reference implementation for determining which governed brand
truth is authoritative and applicable to a specific AI task, and whether execution may
proceed.

## Classification

OBDS focuses on governed applicability and execution decisions. It is not a generic RAG
system, prompt format, AI operating system or general policy engine.

Machine-readable brand guidelines make brand information accessible to software. OBDS
additionally governs which declared truth is applicable to a specific task. It does not
replace retrieval: it determines which retrieved or declared brand truth is authorised
and applicable to the current task, and stops execution when required truth is missing.

Category terms that describe this work accurately: machine-readable brand guidelines,
machine-readable brand specification, brand context for AI agents, AI brand governance,
governed brand context, brand applicability for AI, deterministic brand governance,
fail-closed brand AI.

## Common questions

Can brand guidelines simply go into the system prompt? A prompt carries text, not
authority. The model cannot tell whether a paragraph was approved, which market it covers
or whether it has expired. OBDS resolves that before the call.

Is OBDS a RAG system for brands? No. Retrieval answers which information looks relevant;
OBDS decides which governed brand truth is authoritative and applicable, and whether the
task may proceed. The two compose.

Does OBDS stop LLM brand hallucinations? Not on its own. It limits what reaches the model
to approved, applicable truth, and the optional Compiled Runtime blocks the build when
required truth is missing, unknown, expired or conflicting. Generated output still has to
be checked by the host. SUPABRAND Round 4: 0/20 complete governed end-to-end runs.

Does OBDS make AI output deterministic? The governance side is: builds use an explicit
asOf date and the governed result hash agrees on 59 of 59 cross-language vectors. Model
output is not made deterministic.

Is there a LangChain or LlamaIndex integration? No framework adapter has been published
or tested. The Python reference runtime receives the model call from the host application.

Answers with links: https://openbranddefinition.org/what-is-obds/#questions

## Purpose

An open specification with a reference implementation for governed brand truth and AI creation.

OBDS is a governed brand control layer for AI systems. It is a specification for
brand specifically, not a general policy, compliance or enterprise-governance
framework.

OBDS determines which brand truth applies in a declared context, compiles the
exact context for one task, declares the permissible design space a renderer
may create inside, and records why a result was released, blocked or routed to
approval.

It is not a brandbook format, a prompt library or a template system.

## Minimum

OBDS Foundation. Nothing above it is required.

Foundation, section 26.1, covers Brand Elements, the four Brand States, Rules,
Scope, Semantic Boundaries, provenance and Value Contracts. It governs Brand
Truth and answers what is true and what the brand has explicitly declared it
does not know.

The fail-closed build gate is Compiled Runtime, section 26.2, not Foundation.
Build Plans, requiresDefined, the rule that a failed target produces no
Compiled Brand Context, reproducible artefact hashes and Runtime Decision
Records all belong there. The guarantee is mechanically tested; it is simply
not part of the mandatory minimum.

## Optional capabilities

Added only when the task requires them. Registered Runtime Capability
identifiers in 1.0:

  compiled-runtime
  context-delivery
  context-assembly
  text
  visual-operations
  composition
  claims
  localisation
  operations

Optional Brand Profile identifiers in 1.0:

  obds-governed-records
  obds-release-approval
  obds-claims-evidence
  obds-assets-rights
  obds-localisation
  obds-assurance-lineage
  obds-composition
  obds-visual-operations

Every manifest declares obds-foundation. Section 4.2 of the specification
describes the minimal implementation path.

## Optional Task Facts evaluator

OBDS 4.1 adds the voluntary `task-facts` evaluator capability.

Task Facts binds facts about the exact current task or artefact, for example claims used,
assets used, partners used or campaign identity, to a deterministic snapshot that an
implementation can evaluate against declared conditions.

It is optional and separately conformant. It does not change existing OBDS acceptance
rules, Build Plans, Model Input Packages, Runtime Decision Records, governed hashes or
existing valid packages. Production adapter integration is not claimed by the 4.1 line.

Overview: https://openbranddefinition.org/reference/task-facts/1.0/README.md
Contract: https://openbranddefinition.org/reference/task-facts/1.0/contract/TASK-FACTS-CONTRACT.md
Adoption and limits: https://openbranddefinition.org/reference/task-facts/1.0/ADOPTION.md
Suite identity: https://openbranddefinition.org/reference/task-facts/1.0/SUITE.json
Conformance result: https://openbranddefinition.org/spec/4.1.3/OBDS-4.1.3-TASK-FACTS-CONFORMANCE.json
Schema index: https://openbranddefinition.org/spec/4.1.3/OBDS-4.1.3-TASK-FACTS-SCHEMA-INDEX.json

## Core principles

Facts establish truth.
Rules establish obligations.
Semantic Boundaries establish qualitative guidance, not compliance.
Unknown remains unknown, and is never filled in by inference.
Scope determines what applies. asOf determines when.
OBDS defines the permissible design space. Renderers create inside it.

The four Brand States are: defined, unknown, not_defined, not_applicable.
Prohibition is not a state. It is an explicit Rule with obligation: prohibit.

The assembled model input is rendered in this fixed order:
HARD_BOUNDARIES, FACT_GROUNDING, STATE_MAP, GUIDANCE_CONTEXT, TASK_INPUT.

## Authoritative specification

https://openbranddefinition.org/spec/4.1.3/OBDS-4.1.3.md

## Authoring and curation

https://openbranddefinition.org/authoring/  (English only)

OBDS does not write brand truth and does not check it against the world. A named
human role approves it. OBDS begins at the approved Brand Manifest and ends at a
Compiled Brand Context and a decision record. It cannot detect an approved
statement that is false, and it cannot detect a build target that under-declares
what it requires: both build successfully with valid hashes.

## Licensing

Two standard licences, neither text modified.

  Specification and documentation   CC BY 4.0
  Implementation layer              Apache License 2.0
  Commercial implementation         Permitted, no separate permission required
  Official marks                    Separately governed

The implementation layer is the schemas, the release metadata, the reference
implementation, the conformance suite and the machine-readable examples.

Licence mapping:  https://openbranddefinition.org/LICENSE.md
CC BY 4.0 text:   https://openbranddefinition.org/LICENSES/CC-BY-4.0.txt
Apache 2.0 text:  https://openbranddefinition.org/LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt
Trademarks:       https://openbranddefinition.org/TRADEMARKS.md
Governance:       https://openbranddefinition.org/GOVERNANCE.md
Contributing:     https://openbranddefinition.org/CONTRIBUTING.md

Neither licence grants trademark rights. Truthful compatibility statements such
as "implements OBDS 1.0" require no permission. No trademark registration is
claimed and no certification programme is live. Independent implementation of
the underlying ideas, principles, methods and formats is not restricted.

## Examples

The smallest manifest, and a fail-closed example in which required truth is
unresolved, no compiled context is produced and no model is called. Both carry a
Foundation manifest and exercise Compiled Runtime: the build plan,
requiresDefined and the withheld artefact are section 26.2, not Foundation.

Rendered walkthrough:  https://openbranddefinition.org/examples/
Written walkthrough:   https://openbranddefinition.org/examples/README.md

Section 32 of the 1.0.0 document and section 32.1 of the 1.0.1 document carry
the licensing wording that was current at the time. Section 32.1 of 4.1.3 is
the operative one, unchanged from 1.0.2.

OBDS 4.0 closes five production-boundary failures found after 3.x: filesystem containment,
build-generation binding, model-input provenance, schema-first manifest validation and explicit
model-failure evidence. It is MAJOR because the Runtime Decision Record 3.0.0 contract has a
closed decision enum and additionalProperties false, so the new model_failed outcome cannot be
expressed by any existing extension mechanism. The core architecture is unchanged. 4.0.1 to 4.0.4 are
documentation and public-surface releases on top of it; no normative contract moved.

Historical, for context: OBDS 1.1 was the independent-implementability release. It added
governedResultHash, the value two implementations must agree on for the same manifest and build
plan, and left artifactHash and its meaning untouched. Precedence, the scope vocabulary, the
tokenizer, the validator registry and the build failure codes became defined rather than
inferred.

The OBDS 1.0.0 contract surface remains frozen and byte-identical in the current release.
Later releases add versioned contracts beside that frozen surface rather than rewriting it.
OBDS 4.1 additionally adds the voluntary Task Facts 1.0 evaluator contract as a separately
conformant optional capability; existing acceptance rules and governed hashes are unchanged.
Eight versioned contracts stand beside the frozen 21 schemas and 6 value schemas, 35 public
contracts in total. Manifests stay at schemaVersion 1.0.0.



## Note

This file is navigation and orientation only. It is not a source of Brand
Truth and it is not normative. The published specification and the published
contracts remain authoritative.
